correctness.rationale: For an ideal element with finite group support, ad_X acts diagonally on each g component with eigenvalue c(g), so polynomial Lagrange spectral projections isolate all finite c-level blocks within the ideal. Multiply each block by an appropriate u_h^(-1) to land in I cap C[X]. For F in this ideal, conjugating by a q with c(q)=a0 !=0 and subtracting F(X-a0)-F(X) decreases its degree with leading coefficient -n a0 b_n. Characteristic zero makes -n a0 invertible; induction forces all coefficients b_n to lie in J=I cap C, yielding I cap C[X]=J[X], hence I=AJ. The coset and polynomial grading gives AJ cap C=J; the same argument shows Z(A)=C. Centrality and faithful graded extension preserve ideal products; prime and maximal correspond. Char p G=Z,c(1)=1: shift fixes X^p-X and its principal two-sided ideal is proper, with zero intersection with k ker c=k[u_p,u_p^(-1)] (the kernel here is pZ). No finite computation substitutes for this all-G proof.
residual_risks: No new verifier source: proof checked symbolically by finite-support ad_X and degree induction, not computationally formalized.
Positive characteristic counterexample requires remembering ker c=pZ, not the trivial group.

value.rationale: The exact ideal lattice, center, prime/maximal spectrum and product structure of this natural infinite skew group algebra are a structural classification, beyond the graded ideal theory in its motivating Ore paper. The sharp positive-characteristic counterexample identifies the precise mechanism of failure, providing an independently reusable algebraic criterion.
residual_risks: The result is restricted to a translation action with abelian G and characteristic zero, not arbitrary Ore or skew group rings.

final_claim: For any char-0 field k, abelian G, nonzero additive homomorphism c:G->(k,+), the translation skew group algebra A=k[X]rtimes G with u_g X=(X-c(g))u_g has center C=k ker c, and contraction/extension are inverse product-preserving lattice isomorphisms between all two-sided ideals of A and ideals of C, including prime/maximal spectra. For finitely generated free G, C is a Laurent polynomial ring. In char p, translation-invariant X^p-X supplies a failure.
limitations: char k=0, abelian G, c nonzero; no general nonabelian or char-p ideal lattice statement.
Full Mihovski 2001 and Ait Mohamed 2026 primary texts inaccessible, material originality risk persists.
